thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Higher as Inflation Data, China's Stimulus Moves Offset Disappointing JP Morgan Earnings

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Higher as Inflation Data, China's Stimulus Moves Offset Disappointing JP Morgan Earnings
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Tuesday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +1%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +1.2%
ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ): -5.9%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.9%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +2%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 2%.
US stocks turned positive at session's half, as inflation data and efforts from China to spur economic growth offset disappointing earnings results from JP Morgan (JPM).
JP Morgan earlier reported Q4 earnings and revenue that both fell short of analysts' expectations. The firm also said revenue from fixed-income, commodity and currency (FICC) trading fell to its lowest level since the financial crisis.
Set in motion by Beijing's plans to cut taxes to boost the economy, European bourses all closed higher ahead of Tuesday's pivotal Brexit vote. At 2 pm ET, the UK parliament will finally vote on a bill dictating the terms of Britain's exit from the European Union. If the House of Commons votes against the bill (which is expected), Prime Minister Theresa May has until Monday to present a backup plan. If the backup plan is not approved by March 29, the UK could face a divorce from the EU without a deal.
Power Play: Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was up 1.6%, while other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were higher. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 1.5%.
Kitov Pharmaceuticals Holdings (KTOV) soared some 133% after the biopharmaceutical company reported new findings from its ongoing collaboration with the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, which demonstrated the anti-cancer effect of NT219. Results of the study showed that a short exposure of cancerous cells to NT219 was sufficient to trigger irreversible shutdown to cancer pathways.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.9%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 2.8% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was down 2.7%.
First Republic Bank (FRC) rose nearly 12% after the firm reported Q4 earnings that topped but revenue that missed Wall Street expectations. EPS increased 17.3% to 1.29 in the December quarter, from $1.10 in the year-earlier period. That surpassed the $1.22 average estimate of analysts surveyed by Capital IQ. Q4 revenue increased 16% to $810.8 million but trailed the CapIQ consensus of $812.1 million.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 1.6%, while tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the green.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 1.3% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.8%.
The US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit on Monday upheld a judgment that has grown to $440 million in value in favor of VirnetX (VHC), denying Apple's (AAPL) appeal. The jury verdict was originally valued at $302 million, but it has since grown with interest, enhanced damages, and other costs. The intellectual property licensing firm VirnetX won the judgment against Apple in 2016. The same patent claims have been deemed invalid by an administrate court, but VirnetX is currently appealing those findings. The two companies have sparred over patents since 2010. AAPL rose nearly 2%.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was up 0.6% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.5%.
MagneGas (MNGA) fell 1% after the alternative energy company said it has generated sales of $1 million in December, up 212% from the $0.3 million in the same period last year. "Overall, December is historically the slowest sales month for MagneGas, impacted primarily due to the holiday season," the company said. "Given both Christmas and New Years' holidays occurred mid-week in 2018, MagneGas lost three out of 23 business days to observe those holidays for its employees during the month."
Commodities
Crude was up 2.6%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 2.2%. Natural gas down 1.2% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 1.4%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.3%. Silver was down 0.5%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.4%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 1% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were higher
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was up 1% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were firmer.
Blue Apron Holdings (APRN) surged after the company said it is confident it will post a profitable Q1 and FY19 on an adjusted EBITDA basis. Blue Apron is set to release its financial results for Q4 and 2018 on Jan. 31.
